compile. The generator understands interfaces with inheritance, partial
interfaces, mixins and includes, dictionaries (flattened, inherited
members first and each level by name, as WebIDL reads them), enums,
callbacks, callback interfaces, typedefs, constants, attributes,
operations with overloads, optional arguments with defaults and variadic
ones, constructors, static members, getters, setters and deleters,
`iterable<>` and stringifiers; an interface with an indexed getter of
its own and no `iterable<>` iterates as an array (WebIDL: its
`@@iterator` is `%Array.prototype.values%`), so `for...of` over an
HTMLCollection or a NamedNodeMap works. Reflected attributes need no code: an
extended attribute names the content attribute and kind (`[Reflect]`,
`[Reflect=for]`, `[ReflectURL]`, `[ReflectEnum=(...)]` with
`[ReflectMissing]`/`[ReflectInvalid]`, `[ReflectDefault]`,
`[ReflectPositive]`), and `[LocalNames=(...)]` says which HTML elements
get an interface. Attributes of type EventHandler are event handlers,
also without code.

**The dispatcher** (`Web.Bindings.Dispatch`): every member becomes a
native function (or an accessor pair) whose data is its table row and
whose magic number is the declaring interface. The entry checks the
brand (a wrapper of the interface or a descendant, by the parent table;
the global object is the window), picks the overload by argument count,
converts the arguments with WebIDL's conversions (`Web.Bindings.Conversions`:
boolean, the integer types with modulo, `[EnforceRange]` and `[Clamp]`,
float and double, DOMString kept as WTF-8 and USVString made proper
UTF-8, ByteString, object, interface types, callback functions and
interfaces, dictionaries with defaults and required members, enums,
sequences through the iterator protocol, records, nullable types and
unions in the standard's order), calls the routine with a `TBindingCall`
(the converted values, this's native object) and turns Pascal exceptions
into script ones: EDomException becomes a DOMException (whose prototype
inherits from Error.prototype), EBindingTypeError and EBindingRangeError
TypeError and RangeError, EScriptEnvironmentUnsupported a
NotSupportedError. Attributes add `[SameObject]` (the value cached in a
slot of the wrapper), `[PutForwards]`, `[Replaceable]`, reflection
(`Web.Bindings.Reflection`: strings, URLs against the document's base
URL, booleans, the HTML rules for integers and floats with defaults,
enumerated attributes) and event handlers. Interfaces with indexed or
named getters (NodeList, HTMLCollection, NamedNodeMap, DOMTokenList,
DOMStringMap, CSSStyleDeclaration's indices) have exotic wrappers
(`Web.Bindings.Exotic`) answering the internal methods as WebIDL's legacy
platform objects do, with the named property visibility rules,
`[LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties]` and `[LegacyOverrideBuiltIns]`.
Interface objects are made when first needed (a wrapper of the
interface, or a script reading its name, which is an accessor on the
global object until then), parents first; the window's members are the
global object's own and its prototype becomes Window.prototype.

**Wrappers and lifetime** (`Web.Bindings.Context`). A wrapper is a
`TBindingWrapper` (a host object) whose native object is a node, an
event, an object a node owns (childNodes, children, classList,
attributes, dataset), or an object of its own (a static NodeList, a URL,
a TextDecoder):

- A node has one wrapper, made the first time script sees it and kept in
  the node's ScriptWrapper slot; the wrapper holds a reference to the
  node (Retain/Release), so a node lives at least as long as its wrapper.
  Events the same with TEvent's new reference count (an event freed
  while its wrapper lives leaves the wrapper without a native object
  instead of dangling).
- The node's slot does not keep its wrapper alive. Nodes keep wrappers
  alive by groups: a node's group is the root of its tree (the document
  for a connected node, the root of a detached subtree; an Attr is in its
  element's group, template contents in the template's). After the
  collector has marked from the roots, a weak processor finds the groups
  with a marked wrapper and marks every other wrapper of those groups,
  until nothing more is marked (each wrapper's group root is computed
  once per collection, the live groups are a hash set). The window's
  document wrapper is a root, so every wrapper of a connected node lives
  with its expandos, listeners and handlers as long as its node is in
  the document, and script never sees two wrappers of one node (WeakMaps
  keyed by nodes keep working).
- Cycles through the DOM need nothing special: a detached subtree whose
  wrappers refer only to each other (expandos, listeners closing over
  nodes) has no wrapper marked from outside, so its whole group dies in
  one collection; the wrappers' destructors release their nodes and the
  DOM's CollectGarbage, between tasks, frees the subtree. A dying node
  wrapper disables its node's script listeners, so the DOM never calls a
  dead function.
- Script listeners (`TScriptEventListener` in the DOM's listener lists)
  and event handlers are marked by their target's wrapper; the window's
  by the context's root provider, which also marks the wrappers of events
  being dispatched. Objects owned by a node keep their owner's wrapper
  (and so the node) alive.
- On x86-64 a node wrapper costs 152 bytes (the host object, a registry
  index, the [SameObject] slots made on demand and the owner value); a
  new window about 420 KB of script heap over the bare realm (the
  window's and the document's interfaces; the others when used).

**Interfaces.** EventTarget (with capture, once, passive, handleEvent
objects), Event, CustomEvent, UIEvent, MouseEvent, KeyboardEvent,
FocusEvent, InputEvent (`Web.Dom.UiEvents` has their native classes for
the input code); Node, Document, DOMImplementation, DocumentFragment,
DocumentType, CharacterData, Text, CDATASection, Comment,
ProcessingInstruction, Attr, Element with the ParentNode, ChildNode and
NonDocumentTypeChildNode mixins; innerHTML, outerHTML,
insertAdjacentHTML; querySelector, querySelectorAll, matches and closest
through libcss's parser and matcher (`Web.Bindings.Selectors` has a
small element adapter, to be merged with the style system's; parsed
selectors are cached); HTMLElement and about seventy element interfaces,
mostly reflection, with click() and its checkbox activation, focus
events, dataset, style (`Web.Bindings.Style`: CSSStyleDeclaration over
the style attribute with libcss's declaration parser and serializer;
the properties by camel-cased, dashed and -webkit- names are answered by
the wrapper rather than an accessor pair each), the hyperlink URL parts,
form controls' value and checkedness with their dirty flags, radio
groups, select and option selectedness, constraint validation basics,
form.elements and GET submission (`Web.Bindings.FormControls`); NodeList,
HTMLCollection, HTMLOptionsCollection, NamedNodeMap, DOMTokenList,
DOMStringMap, DOMException; Window (window, self, document, location,
history, navigator, the prompts, viewport metrics, origin, atob, btoa,
the timers, structuredClone, getComputedStyle), Location (its setters navigate),
History and Navigator; TextEncoder and TextDecoder over libweb's decoders
(fatal, ignoreBOM, streaming); URL and URLSearchParams over libhttp's
`Url.*`; MutationObserver and MutationRecord. console and queueMicrotask
are libjavascript's (console output goes to the context's
OnConsoleMessage).

**MutationObserver** (`Web.Bindings.MutationObservers`) takes the
document observer's records: registrations (an observer, a node, the
options; transient ones for removed nodes of observed subtrees until the
next notification) are matched on the target's inclusive ancestors and
each interested observer gets its record, with the old value if one of
its registrations asked; the first record queues the mutation observer
microtask as a libjavascript job.

**Scripts** (`Web.Script.Context`). `TScriptContext` is the window: it
installs the interfaces, observes the document (event handler content
attributes, script elements, mutation observers), and is the parser's
script host (`TParserScriptHost`). Script elements go through
`PrepareScript`, the standard's "prepare the script element" (type and
language checks, already started, parser-inserted, nomodule scripts run
because modules do not exist yet): inline classic scripts run at once,
external ones go to the environment with their mode (parser-blocking
ones pause the parser). It runs at the parser's script end tags and for
script elements that become connected or get their text while
connected (not innerHTML's, whose scripts are marked already started).
`ExecuteClassicScript(Source, Url, Element)` runs a script with
document.currentScript set, reports an uncaught exception to the
console with the file and line ("page.html (inline script 3)"), fires
an external script's load event, and leaves through the microtask
checkpoint (the job queue, mutation observers included; at script depth
0 only, as in "clean up after running script").
The outermost entry into script (`EnterScript`, module evaluation too)
arms the slow script watchdog (`Web.Script.Watchdog`) until it is back
out after the microtask checkpoint: a page's scripts run on the page
thread, the GUI thread in a web view, so a script that never ends would
freeze the window. One thread for the process sleeps while nothing is
armed and otherwise checks every 100 ms; an entry armed longer than
`ScriptRunLimitMilliseconds` (10 s; the display server calls a window
"Not responding" after 5) gets the engine's `InterruptRequested` set,
again on every check while it stays armed, so the interpreter ends the
script at its next backward jump or call with an uncatchable
termination, and the promise jobs it queued end the same way; the
console says the script was stopped, and the page's next scripts run as
usual (WebScriptTest checks a loop, one inside try, promise jobs queueing
each other and a looping timer callback). document.write goes to
the active parser at its insertion point (the parser now saves the old
insertion point and limit of nested scripts and writes, so scripts
written by scripts write in the right place). Outside the parser
document.open empties the document and starts a script-created parser
that document.write feeds and document.close finishes (readyState,
DOMContentLoaded and load follow; its scripts run in that document's
window even under a loader): an iframe's about:blank document written
by its parent, as DuckDuckGo does to follow some links; a write after
loading opens the document anew, as in other engines. Event handler IDL
attributes and content attributes (`Web.Bindings.EventHandlers`) keep
their functions in the target wrapper's handler slot; a content
attribute is compiled as the body of `function on<type>(event)` when
first needed and again after it changes; each target registers one
listener per handler type, keeping its place among the listeners;
returning false cancels. `ParseDocument(Html)` parses a whole page with
its scripts, then fires readystatechange, DOMContentLoaded and the
window's load event.

**What the rest of the engine provides** (`Web.ScriptEnvironment`): the
loader and the event loop subclass `TScriptEnvironment` and pass it to
the context. Hooks they implement (a hook left alone raises
EScriptEnvironmentUnsupported, a NotSupportedError for scripts; the
timers are removed from the window unless `SupportsTimers`):

- `SupportsTimers`, `StartTimer(Context, Id, Milliseconds, Repeating)`,
  `StopTimer`: the loop calls `TScriptContext.FireTimer(Id)` as a task
  when due (the context keeps the handlers, arguments and nesting).
- `FetchClassicScript(Context, Element, Url, Charset, Mode)`: fetch, then
  `ExecuteClassicScript` (or `ScriptFetchFailed`) in the mode's order;
  after a parser-blocking one, `Parser.Resume`.
- `LocationHref`, `Navigate(Url, ReplaceEntry)`, `Reload`,
  `HistoryLength`, `HistoryGo`, `HistoryChangeUrl` (pushState and
  replaceState; the context changes document.URL and keeps the state).
- `Alert`, `Confirm`, `Prompt`; `ViewportWidth`, `ViewportHeight`,
  `DevicePixelRatio`; `GetCookies`, `SetCookie`; `UserAgent`, `Language`.
- The loader drives a page in pieces with `BeginParsing(Parser)`,
  `FinishParsing` (interactive, DOMContentLoaded) and `DocumentLoaded`
  (complete, load), and calls `PerformMicrotaskCheckpoint` after each
  task it runs.

**Scripts in loaded pages** (`Web.Script.PageScripting`): a page's
`TPageScriptExecutor` (the loader's `TScriptExecutor`, made by the web
view for its page) and its `TPageScriptEnvironment` join the two sides.
The loader tells its executor when a document starts, stops (aborted:
being left) and goes (`DocumentStarted`, `DocumentStopped`,
`DocumentFreed`, virtual hooks of `TScriptExecutor` called by
`TDocumentLoader`), and the executor makes the document's
`TScriptContext` with the loader's `TWebWindow` as the window (a binding
context takes a window event target now; without one it makes its own),
so the loader's events (DOMContentLoaded, load, pageshow) and the
page's listeners and `on...` handlers meet. The loader prepares,
fetches and orders script elements (parser-blocking, deferred, async,
script-inserted in order, modules) and hands each to `ExecuteScript`;
the context does not prepare scripts itself (`PreparesScripts` False)
and document.readyState is the document's (`ReadyStateFromDocument`).
While a parser-inserted script runs, document.write goes to the loader's
parser (`AttachParser`). Module scripts run through the engine's
`EvaluateModule` with a resolver (specifiers against the importing
module's URL; bare ones through the document's import maps,
`Web.Script.ImportMaps`: imports, "/"-ending prefixes, scopes with the
most specific covering the referrer first, null entries blocking a
specifier, maps merged as they arrive with entries already there kept;
the JSON read with the engine's JSON.parse) and a fetcher
that asks the loader (`TScriptScheduler.FetchScript`: CORS, UTF-8), one
pair per context. The loop's microtask checkpoint runs every live
context's jobs. The environment: timers as the loop's delayed tasks
grouped by context (they stop with its document); location; navigation
with the page as its source; history.go as a history traversal task;
pushState and replaceState through `TNavigable.ChangeUrlFromScript` (a
new entry of the same document, or the current one); prompts as events
(`OnAlert`, `OnConfirm`, `OnPrompt`: the web view's page waits while a
dialog is open); the console (`OnConsoleMessage`); the viewport and
pixel ratio from the resource sink's media environment; document.cookie
through the network context's jar (HttpOnly cookies neither read nor
replaced); the user agent and language. Because the bindings' units use
each other in a cycle, libweb is compiled a second time from
`Web.Script.PageScripting`, so programs that use them find consistent
units. querySelector, matches and closest match through the style
system's element adapter (`Web.Style.Adapter`), so script sees the
hover, active and focus states the web view sets.

**Nested windows (iframes)** (`Web.Script.Frames`). An iframe element
that becomes connected in a scripted document gets a window of its own:
a `TScriptContext` made with `CreateFrame`, whose engine is another
realm in the parent's runtime (`TJsEngine.CreateSharing`). Objects and
functions pass freely between the realms, and each function runs in the
realm it was made in (libjavascript dispatches calls on a function's
`Realm`; a built-in made in a frame creates its objects there, an
`Array` species of another realm makes an array of the current one).
The first document is about:blank (html, head and body, the parent's
origin and cookies) or the srcdoc markup parsed with its scripts; the
iframe's load event fires then. contentWindow, contentDocument,
window.parent, top, frameElement and length follow; removing the
element closes the window (`Close`: its realm stops being a root and is
detached; what the parent kept still works, running in the caller's
realm). Frames are freed with their top-level context, after its engine
(their cells live in its runtime). `TFrameEnvironment` forwards timers,
prompts, cookies, storage, fetches and the user agent to the parent's
environment. That is the script-only path (an environment that does not
manage frames: tests, `ParseDocument`); a page's frames are child
navigables (below).

**Frames of a page** (`Web.Navigation.Navigables.Frames.inc`,
`Web.Navigation.FramePolicy`, `Web.Script.FrameNavigables`,
`Web.Bindings.CrossOrigin`, `Web.Frames.Views`). Each `<iframe>` and
`<frame>` that becomes connected in a navigable's active document gets a
child `TNavigable` (`CreateChild`) at once - the loader's observer
reports frame elements (`OnFrameInserted`, `OnFrameChanged` for src,
srcdoc and name, `OnFrameRemoved`) - with an initial about:blank
document of the parent's origin, so contentWindow works right after the
insertion; then the iframe's attributes are processed as the HTML
Standard says: srcdoc navigates to about:srcdoc in a task, src to its
URL against the parent's base URL (about:blank at the first insertion
only fires load, at once), `loading=lazy` waits for the parent's load
event, a URL of an ancestor's document or a ninth level is not loaded.
The navigation request is the parent document's (its client: origin,
referrer and policy, the top-level site that SameSite cookies are
judged by), destination iframe or frame, the element's referrerpolicy;
a response that X-Frame-Options (DENY, SAMEORIGIN against every
ancestor) or an enforced CSP `frame-ancestors` (which decides when
present) keeps out shows an error page. The sandbox attribute as it is
at each navigation: without allow-scripts the document gets no script
executor, without allow-same-origin an opaque origin (no cookies, no
storage), without allow-modals no prompts; nested frames keep their
ancestors' restrictions; `allow` is kept, not enforced. While a child
loads it delays its parent's load event (lazy ones do not); when its
document has loaded, load fires at the element. Documents carry their
origin when it is not their URL's (`TDocument.OriginText`,
`Web.Origins`: about:blank and srcdoc documents their creator's, opaque
ones stable per document). A navigation while the child or its parent
is still loading replaces the child's entry; a later one adds one to
the child's history and one naming the child (`FrameId`, `FrameIndex`)
to the top-level history, the joint session history: Back and Forward
over such entries traverse the child (`TraverseFrames`), history.length
and history.go in a frame are the joint history's. The element leaving
or its document being unloaded detaches the child at once (loading
stopped, its windows closed, its rendering withdrawn) and frees it in a
later task. `ChooseNavigable` gives a link's or form's target (_self,
_parent, _top, a frame's name; nil for _blank or an unknown name, a new
tab).

A child document's script context is made by the page's executor with
`CreateFrame` in a realm of its parent's engine and the child's window
(`TNavigableFrameEnvironment`: the page's environment for timers,
cookies, storage, fetches and prompts with the frame's own context, the
child navigable for location, navigation, pushState, the viewport and
media queries, a `TFrameScriptLayout` for geometry). Cross-origin frames
share the heap too (one runtime per page: objects cannot be passed
between heaps, and postMessage's source, frames[i] and parent stay plain
references); what keeps origins apart is that a window's global object
is never handed to script of another origin: contentWindow, parent,
top, frames[i] and a message's source go through `WindowValueFor`,
which gives a cross-origin view (`TCrossOriginWindowView`, an exotic
object of the asking realm, cached per pair) answering only window,
self, frames, top, parent, opener, closed, length, the frames by index,
location (a view whose href may be set and replace() called),
postMessage, close, focus and blur, undefined for then and the three
symbols, a SecurityError for anything else; contentDocument and
frameElement are null across origins. postMessage through a view calls
the target's own and turns its exceptions into the caller's realm's.
MessagePorts go between realms of any origins without carrying their
realm: the receiving realm's postMessage asks the caller's realm (the
native `exportPorts`, its `CallerRealm`'s platform callback) for
endpoints of the transferred ports, frozen objects without a prototype
whose functions clone what they are given into their own realm; the
sending port stays behind as a relay and the receiver gets a port of
its own realm (`platform/60-messaging.js`). Within one realm a
transferred port is replaced by a new object and the old one is dead
(a second transfer is a DataCloneError). Workers' and ports' own
postMessage carry ports too. reCAPTCHA needs both: its anchor frame
talks to its worker and to the page through ports, and timed out after
5 and 15 s showing "Could not connect to the reCAPTCHA service" when
they did not arrive (on the host as well as in QEMU: webbrowse quit
before the timeouts). Frames are also found by name: window[name] and
frames[name] (`UpdateFrameIndices` defines them below the window's own
properties; cross-origin views answer them), which reCAPTCHA's challenge
frame uses to reach its anchor. A frame's window
is closed when its document is left (contentWindow is then the next
document's) and freed with its top-level context. The global object's
index properties follow its frames (`UpdateFrameIndices`). A
sandboxed frame without scripts has no window object (frames.length
does not count it).

Rendering: `TLayoutResourceSink.CreateChildSink` gives each child a
rendering sink and a `TFrameView` (its navigable observer): per
document a `TDocumentLayout` and `TDocumentPainter`, registered in the
parent document's resources under the element as a `TEmbeddedContent`
(`Web.Layout.EmbeddedContent`). The parent's layout gives it the
frame's content box (300 by 150 without a ratio by default; width,
height, CSS, the UA sheet's 2px inset border, `frameborder=0`) and its
scale (zoom and DPI inherited) and brings it up to date after its own
layout; its paint version includes the frames'. The builder emits a
`diFrame` item and the raster asks the frame to paint itself into the
visible part of its box (`PaintShifted`: the view's `ShiftX`/`ShiftY`),
with a thin scroll bar when the document overflows (not with
`scrolling="no"`). `HitTestThroughFrames` descends into frames and
`DocumentViewportOrigin` says where a frame's viewport is. With a null
sink (tests) children load without views.

**Workers** (`platform/65-workers.js`, `Web.Script.NativeWorkers`).
`new Worker(url)` fetches the script and runs it in a bare realm of the
window's runtime (its own built-ins, no DOM: `TBindingContext.
WorkerEngines`, whose jobs run at the window's checkpoints) on the
window's thread. The scope has self, location, navigator, name,
postMessage, close, the listener methods and onmessage, and the
window's timers, fetch, crypto, performance, console, encoders, URLs,
blobs, streams and messaging classes; messages are structured clones in
tasks; uncaught errors fire error at the Worker. importScripts cannot
wait for a fetch on this thread: one with scripts not yet fetched stops
the worker's script, fetches them (through fetch(), so CORS applies) and
runs the script again from the start in a new scope (reCAPTCHA's
webworker.js is one importScripts line).

**Platform scripts** (`Web.Script.Natives`, `userland/lib/web/platform/*.js`).
Interfaces that are mostly object juggling and promises over a few engine
services are written in JavaScript: `make-bindings.py` turns the files
into `Web.Script.PlatformSources.inc`, and every window runs them in file
name order, as built-ins (`TJsEngine.EvaluateBuiltin`: their functions
read as `function f() { [native code] }`). Each is a function of the
natives object, the global object and a shared `internal` object;
classes come out WebIDL-like (`internal.finishInterface`: accessors and
methods on the prototype, a toStringTag, "Illegal constructor" for
interfaces script cannot make). The natives are Pascal routines of the
window's context (a guarded table: a Pascal exception becomes a script
error) over `TScriptEnvironment`:

| File | What it gives |
|---|---|
| 00-base | the helpers; event handler attributes of platform interfaces; ProgressEvent |
| 10-performance | Performance (now, timeOrigin, timing, navigation, entries, marks, measures), PerformanceObserver, PerformanceNavigationTiming from the loader's moments |
| 20-storage | Storage, localStorage and sessionStorage: a proxy over the environment's `TWebStorageArea` (named properties, `in`, Object.keys, the 5 MiB quota) |
| 30-window | Image, Option and Audio factories; requestAnimationFrame at the window's rendering opportunities (a 16 ms beat without them); requestIdleCallback; Screen; matchMedia with change events; the CSS namespace (supports through libcss, escape); Crypto (getRandomValues, randomUUID, subtle.digest with libcryptography); navigator plugins, mime types, permissions, sendBeacon |
| 35-fonts | FontFace, FontFaceSet, document.fonts (settled at once: style sheets' fonts are the loader's) |
| 40-streams-blobs | ReadableStream (default readers, tee, pipes, async iteration), WritableStream, TransformStream, TextDecoderStream and TextEncoderStream; Blob, File, FileReader, blob: URLs; FormData |
| 50-fetch | AbortController and AbortSignal (abort, timeout, any), Headers (guards, forbidden names), Request, Response (the body mixin, clone with tee), fetch(), XMLHttpRequest (asynchronous; all response types) |
| 60-messaging | postMessage with the calling window as source (libjavascript notes the caller realm of a cross-realm call), MessageEvent, MessageChannel, MessagePort, BroadcastChannel |
| 70-geometry | DOMRect, DOMPoint, getBoundingClientRect, getClientRects (an inline element's line fragments, `Web.Layout.BoxGeometry`; moved by position: relative, translation and the scroll containers above), client*, scroll*, offset*, scrolling, scrollIntoView, the window's scroll position, elementFromPoint, scrollingElement, getComputedStyle |
| 71-traversal | NodeFilter, TreeWalker and NodeIterator (createTreeWalker, createNodeIterator) over the bindings' own tree getters, so a polyfill that redefines firstChild does not change what they walk |
| 72-selection | Range.getClientRects and getBoundingClientRect (the layout's line fragments of the text in the range, the boxes of the elements in it: `TScriptLayout.TextRects`); selectionchange, once a task for any number of changes |
| 74-cssom | CSSStyleSheet.replace (replaceSync, then a settled promise) |
| 75-observers | IntersectionObserver and ResizeObserver (checked after observe() and every 200 ms while something is observed) |

The environment hooks they use (`Web.ScriptEnvironment`):
`NavigationTiming`, `StorageArea` and `StorageChanged`,
`MediaEnvironment`, `ScreenWidth`/`ScreenHeight`,
`RequestAnimationFrame`, `SendBeacon`, `StartFetch`/`CancelFetch` with a
`TScriptFetchSink`, and `Layout`, a `TScriptLayout` that answers geometry
and computed values (`Web.Script.Layout` answers from a
`TDocumentLayout` after bringing it up to date; the web view and
webbrowse set one). The page environment implements them: navigation
timing from `TLoadingContext.Times` (the navigable notes the navigation
start, response start and protocol, the loader DOM interactive, the
DOMContentLoaded and load events; the window's time origin is the
navigation start); local storage per origin from the host's
`TWebStorageRegistry` (a file per origin, saved a second after a change;
the browser keeps it in ~/.settings/browser/storage), session storage
per page; script fetches over the loader's fetch layer
(`Web.Script.PageFetch`: CORS, credentials, cookies, the cache; the
response filtered as the Fetch Standard says: no Set-Cookie, CORS
responses with the safelisted and exposed headers only, opaque ones with
status 0 and no headers); beacons as keepalive no-cors POSTs outside the
document's fetch group; animation frames as the window's frame
callbacks.

**Forms and focus in the DOM.** A form control's state that is not in
its attributes (value and its dirty flag, checkedness, selectedness, the
text selection) lives with the element (`Web.Dom.FormControls`, in the
node's rare data), so the bindings, the web view and the styler see one
value; changing it tells the document's observers
(`ControlStateChanged`: :checked and :placeholder-shown restyle, the
painter shows the value). Inputs and text areas have selectionStart,
selectionEnd, selectionDirection, setSelectionRange and select(). Focus
is the document's (`TDocument.FocusedElement`, `Web.Dom.Focus`: which
elements are focusable areas, and the focusing steps with blur,
focusout, focus and focusin carrying relatedTarget); focus(), blur(),
document.activeElement and the web view all go through it, and the
view follows the document (`FocusChanged`).

The user agent is `Mozilla/5.0 (X11; FreePascalOS x86_64)
AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) libweb/1.0 Safari/537.36`
(aarch64 on ARM; `WebView.Network`, the script environment's default
the same): it names the platform and the engine, and carries the
compatibility tokens every engine sends, without which sites send
reduced pages (Google answers a bare "libweb" with its basic page and
"Update your browser" for search).

**Google search.** The home page loads without script errors; typing
in the search box (Google's textarea, focused by its script) and Enter
go through its keydown handler and form submission; the results URL
answers with the "SearchGuard" challenge, whose BotGuard program runs
(it needs an about:blank iframe's realm for pristine built-ins). With
the same clock, random numbers and cookies the challenge's token is byte
for byte the token Firefox computes (checked on the host with an
instrumented copy of the page, the engine and Firefox side by side);
Google then redirects this engine to its CAPTCHA page ("unusual
traffic", /sorry/index), whose reCAPTCHA widget needs src iframes.

Events the engine fires are released, never freed (a listener that
touches one makes a wrapper holding a reference: the collector read
freed events, the DuckDuckGo crash), keep isTrusted (only script's
dispatchEvent clears it), and hold only node targets: the window,
XMLHttpRequest, AbortSignal and other targets belong to their wrappers,
which the event's wrapper keeps alive (an event freed after its target
called it back). Promises rejected with no handler are reported to the
console ("Uncaught (in promise) ...") after a microtask checkpoint.
DOMParser parses text/html without scripting (the XML types give a
parsererror document); elements in the SVG namespace are SVGElement,
SVGGraphicsElement or SVGSVGElement with style, dataset, tabIndex,
focus and blur (the HTMLOrSVGElement and ElementCSSInlineStyle mixins).
Location's setters (href, protocol, host, hostname, port, pathname,
search, hash) navigate, so window.location = url works. HTML's cloning
steps: a cloned script that already ran does not run again, cloned
inputs and textareas keep their value and checkedness.

**Ranges and the selection** (`Web.Dom.Ranges.inc`, `Web.Dom.Selection.inc`,
`Web.Dom.RangeContents`, `Web.Bindings.Ranges`). A `TLiveRange` is two
boundary points kept valid by the mutation algorithms: the document
lists its live ranges and insert, remove, replace data (and setting the
data), splitText and normalize adjust them as the DOM Standard says (a
document with no ranges pays one comparison). Ranges are reference
counted; they hold references to their boundary nodes, except the
document's selection range, which is always in its document (the
document must not keep itself alive through it; when the document goes
the range lets go of its nodes). Range has the boundary setters and
checks (IndexSizeError, InvalidNodeTypeError), collapse, selectNode(Contents),
compareBoundaryPoints, comparePoint, isPointInRange, intersectsNode,
cloneContents, extractContents, deleteContents, insertNode,
surroundContents, cloneRange, createContextualFragment and its text;
StaticRange its points. A range has one wrapper (the selection's range
read twice is the same object). The document's `TDocumentSelection` is
one range or none and a direction: getSelection (window and document)
gives the window's one Selection with anchor and focus, type,
direction, getRangeAt, addRange (the range itself becomes the
selection's), removeRange, removeAllRanges, collapse, setPosition,
collapseToStart/End, extend, setBaseAndExtent, selectAllChildren,
containsNode, deleteFromDocument and toString (modify does nothing yet).
Every change tells the document's observers (`SelectionChanged`): the
script context queues selectionchange, the web view repaints. The web
view's text selection is the document's: the user's selection becomes
a DOM range and a range script makes is painted (`WebView.SelectionMapping`
maps a place in the painted text to a node and offset and back;
`Web.Layout.TextOffsets` walks a text node's data against its box's
rendered text across collapsed white space).

**The CSSOM** (`Web.Bindings.StyleSheets`, `Web.Style.DocumentSheets`).
Script and styling share the sheet objects: a document's
`TDocumentSheets` (made on demand, freed with the document) parses each
`<style>`'s sheet when first asked for (script right after inserting
the element, or the styler) and again when its text or media changes,
mirrors the `<link>` sheets the resources own, and keeps the sheets
script makes and the adopted ones (which come after the document's).
document.styleSheets, a style or link element's sheet, CSSStyleSheet
(cssRules, insertRule, deleteRule, the legacy rules, addRule and
removeRule, replaceSync, replace, the constructor with baseURL, media
and disabled), adoptedStyleSheets (a plain array: assigning it takes
effect, changing it in place does not), StyleSheet's ownerNode, href,
title, media and disabled, MediaList, CSSRuleList, and CSSRule with
cssText, parentRule, parentStyleSheet and type; CSSStyleRule
(selectorText, style), CSSGroupingRule (cssRules, insertRule,
deleteRule), CSSMediaRule, CSSSupportsRule, CSSLayerBlockRule,
CSSImportRule, CSSNamespaceRule, CSSFontFaceRule, CSSKeyframesRule
(name, cssRules, appendRule, deleteRule, findRule) and CSSKeyframeRule
(keyText, style). A sheet's or rule's one wrapper is in its HostData;
libcss tells the wrapper when the object is freed (`CssHostDataFreed`).
Changes go to the document's sheets: a rule inserted at the end of a
sheet (what emotion and styled-components do, rule after rule) is
indexed at once when that sheet is the last in effect
(`TCssStyleEngine.AppendRule` adds its selectors after every other
entry), anything else has the sheets indexed again before the next
style; either way the document is restyled. A rule's style changes its
declaration block in place (the index points at it). Removed rules,
replaced selectors and sheets of removed or reparsed `<style>` elements
are retired and freed once the engine has indexed again.

**Not done yet**: custom elements, ErrorEvent and onerror's arguments, the
event handler scope chain (form, document), the unhandledrejection
event, XML parsing (DOMParser, XHR's responseXML), shadow DOM,
TreeWalker, `<object>` and `<embed>` documents, frameset
layout (`<frame>` loads but is laid out as an inline replaced box),
shared and service workers, synchronous
XMLHttpRequest, Web Animations (CSS animations and transitions run, see
Styling), Selection.modify, @import in insertRule loading its sheet,
ObservableArray for adoptedStyleSheets, the storage event between
windows, images' natural size for script.

### Tests

`make web-test` (in `make test`) builds `tools/WebTest` on the host
against the library's sources. Its tree construction cases are in the
html5lib format (`tools/WebTest/tree-construction/*.dat`, written from
the standard's algorithm: misnested formatting and the adoption agency,
tables and foster parenting, templates, foreign content, character
references, raw text elements, comments, doctypes and document modes,
fragments); each case is parsed whole and again one byte at a time, and
some are checked for the document mode (`#mode`) or for parsing their
serialization again (`#roundtrip`). The other checks cover the decoders
(error cases, in pieces), labels, the prescan and sniffing, the
parser's encoding changes and restarts, the DOM's mutation algorithms
and their errors, UTF-16 offsets, attributes and Attr nodes, ids,
live collections, classList, cloning and comparison, namespaces, the
observer hook, node lifetime, the script hook with document.write and
pausing, innerHTML and friends, event dispatch, and serialization. The
test prints the parser's speed and bytes per node ("perf" lines): on the
build machine about 2.3 million nodes (20 MB of HTML) per second.

### Styling (Web.Style)

libweb styles its DOM with libcss. libweb's atoms cannot be libcss's
(libweb's table starts with the HTML names as constants, libcss's with
its keywords in enum order), so `Web.Style.Atoms` maps each libweb atom
once to the libcss atom of the same name, in an array indexed by the
libweb atom; `TDomElementAdapter` (`Web.Style.Adapter`) then answers the
selector matcher with array reads (local names, namespaces, attribute
names, classes from the element's cached class atoms) and the id atom
kept in the node's data, and allocates nothing per element. The states
of the dynamic pseudo-classes come from the node's data (set by the web
view: hover, focus, active ...) plus those the document gives (links,
disabled/enabled/checked controls, required, read-only, placeholder
shown, open details).

Each styled node has a small record in its `LayoutData` slot
(`Web.Style.NodeData`): its computed style and those of its ::before,
::after and ::marker, its parsed style attribute and presentational
hints, its id atom, its states, dirty bits and its first box. The record
is freed when the node leaves the document.

`TDocumentStyler` (`Web.Style.Resolver`) owns the `TCssStyleEngine`: it
keeps the engine's sheets in step with the document's
(`Web.Style.Sheets`: libcss's HTML user agent sheet, the engine's own
additions for form controls and `center` in `Web.Style.UserAgent`, the
user sheets and then the author sheets in tree order: each `<style>`
parsed here and kept with its text, each `<link rel=stylesheet>`'s sheet
from the document's resources; media attributes become the sheets'
media lists, alternate sheets do not apply; a sheet arriving or going
makes the layout due, `SheetsDirty`, so a page whose only change is a
late sheet restyles). Presentational hints
(`Web.Style.Hints`) follow the HTML Standard's rendering section with
its rules for dimension and legacy color values: body's bgcolor, text,
background and margins; table's width, height, bgcolor, border,
cellspacing and align; cells' width, height, nowrap, align, valign and
the table's cellpadding and border; align on p, div, headings and
captions; img/object/embed/iframe/video/canvas width, height, align,
border, hspace, vspace; hr's width, size, color, noshade and align;
font's color, face and size; list types; ol start and li value as the
list-item counter; br clear. SVG elements take their presentation
attributes (libsvg's list) as hints, the outermost `<svg>` also its
width and height (a bare number in pixels), which size its box.

Styling walks the tree top-down with the engine's ancestor bloom filter
(PushAncestor/PopAncestor), visiting only subtrees whose dirty bits say
something changed. The styler is a document observer: an inserted
subtree is marked for styling with its new siblings (structural
selectors), an attribute change restyles the element's subtree and
siblings (a style attribute change only the element), and
`<style>`/`<link>` changes mark the sheets dirty. A change of states
(:hover, :focus, :active ...) restyles only what the selectors reading
those states can reach (libcss's `Css.StateInvalidation`, built with the
rule index: each compound with a state pseudo-class, keyed by its type,
id and classes, as the subject - the element -, left of a descendant or
child combinator - its subtree - or of a sibling combinator - its later
siblings' subtrees; one inside :is()/:where() keyed by its alternatives,
one inside :has() restyles all of them). Moving the pointer changes
:hover on a chain of ancestors, which used to restyle whole subtrees (16
ms a move over a Wikipedia article on the build machine, 2 ms now).
Pseudo-elements are matched with the ancestor filter too. After restyling an
element it compares old and new styles struct by struct (structs are
interned, so pointers compare) and reports the kind of change to the
layout: boxes (display, position, float, generated content, lists),
layout, or paint (the boxes then take the new styles and nothing is laid
out again); a changed inherited group restyles the children.

**Animations and transitions** (`Web.Style.Animations`, libcss's
`Css.Interpolation`, `Css.Easing`, `Css.TransformMatrices`). The styler
hands each element's cascaded style to `TStyleAnimations.Animate`,
which keeps the element's CSS animations (animation-name and the other
animation properties, each name's @keyframes rule; duration, delay,
iteration count, direction, fill mode, play state, easing) and its
transitions (started when a transitioned property's cascaded value
changes, from the value shown at that moment; a new change cancels and
replaces one), and returns the style to show: the cascaded style with
the animated values over it (only the structs that change are copied).
Keyframe values are computed from each keyframe's block alone under the
parent's style (`TCssStyleEngine.ComputeBlockStyle`); missing 0% and
100% frames are the cascaded value. Values interpolate by the
property table's animation type: numbers, integers, lengths and
percentages (mixed ones as length-percentages), colors in
premultiplied sRGB, visibility, font weights, transforms (function by
function when the lists match, none as the other list's identity
functions, otherwise through 2D matrix decomposition); anything else
flips half way. Transitions win over animations. While an element has
effects its cascaded style is kept in its node data (`BaseStyle`); each
frame the owner calls `TDocumentLayout.AdvanceAnimations`, which marks
the elements with running effects `ndAnimationDirty`, and the styler
makes their styles again from the kept base without cascading. Time
is the layout's animation clock (`SetAnimationClock`; GetTickCount64 by
default; the tests set fixed times). Events (animationstart, end,
iteration, cancel; transitionrun, start, end, cancel) are collected
while styling and queued by the owner as tasks
(`Web.Layout.AnimationEvents`: AnimationEvent and TransitionEvent,
bubbling, at elements still in the document). The web view and
webbrowse advance animations and queue their events every frame, and
the view asks for frames while any runs.

### Text (Web.Text)

`Web.Text.Fonts` lists the faces under the font directory (/lib/fonts;
the host tools point it at userland/fonts): a subdirectory per family
("liberation-sans" is "Liberation Sans"), each .ttf, .otf or .ttc file a
face (a collection's first), weight and slant from its header
(`Font.Summaries`, a few hundred bytes read), so a face's file is read
only when it is chosen. Matching walks the font-family list: an
installed family by its name, else what the system's font configuration
(/etc/fonts.conf, see "Fonts" under libfont) says stands for the name:
sans-serif, Arial and Helvetica are Liberation Sans (Arial's metrics),
serif and Times New Roman Liberation Serif, monospace and Courier New
Liberation Mono, Palatino P052 and the other PostScript names their URW
stand-ins, system-ui and -apple-system the interface's DejaVu Sans,
emoji Noto Color Emoji. The face nearest the weight and slant is picked
by the headers and read. A character the face lacks walks the
configured chain for its script (Noto Sans CJK for Han and kana, Noto
Sans Arabic, ..., Noto Color Emoji for emoji) and then the default
chain, each family read only when reached, so mixed text draws every
character (remembered per font and in the library). U+FE0F after a
character asks for the emoji family; any variation selector picks the
face's variation glyph (cmap format 14); selectors and zero-width
joiners take no room (emoji sequences joined by U+200D draw one after
another: there are no ligatures). Colour glyphs paint in their own
colours (`Font.GlyphDrawing`); libweb sets libfont's PNG decoder to
libimage's (`Image.PictureColors`).

A web font face keeps to its `unicode-range` (`Web.Text.UnicodeRanges`):
a family loaded in subsets (latin, latin-ext, cyrillic ...) leads with
the subset for Latin text and draws any other character with the subset
that has it; a character no face of the family has comes from the
default (proportional) family first, then any face that has it.

`TTextFont` (`Web.Text.FontInstances`) is a face at a CSS pixel size,
one per font style struct. Layout measures with the faces' unhinted
advances and kerning scaled exactly, in CSS pixels, so a text has the
same width at every device scale; painting renders glyphs at the device
pixel size from libfont's glyph cache and places them where layout
measured them. Measurements are cached per (font, string) in one hash
table (cleared when full). Bold without a bold face is drawn twice, one
device pixel apart; italic or oblique without such a face is drawn
sheared (a synthetic oblique). `Web.Text.Breaking` has UTF-8 stepping,
text-transform (ASCII, Latin-1, Latin Extended-A, Greek, Cyrillic) and
line break opportunities (a simplified UAX #14: after spaces, U+200B and
hyphens between letters, around ideographs, never before closing
punctuation; word-break break-all and keep-all, line-break anywhere,
no-break spaces).

### Boxes and layout (Web.Layout)

`Web.Layout.TreeBuilder` makes the box tree (`Web.Layout.Boxes`): one box
per element that generates one (display's outer and inner types: block
containers, inline boxes, inline-blocks, flex, grid, the table boxes,
list items with ::marker boxes; replaced boxes for img, video, canvas,
iframe, embed, object, inline svg and the controls the engine draws), one per text
node (not per word or line), ::before/::after with generated text,
`display: contents` giving its children to its parent, `display: none`
nothing. CSS's anonymous boxes: block containers with both block and
inline children wrap inline runs in anonymous blocks (a run of
collapsible white space alone is dropped); flex items are blockified and
text runs among them wrapped; missing table rows, row groups and cells
are made. A block inside an inline box stays there and gets lines of its
own (no inline splitting). `Web.Layout.Counters` applies
counter-reset/set/increment and the list-item counter with CSS Lists 3
scoping in one walk and writes the generated text: strings, counter(),
counters(), attr(), quotes (and the quotes property), markers from
::marker content or list-style-type (the predefined counter styles lists
use) with their suffixes.

A box's border box position is relative to its nearest ancestor that is
not an inline box, in CSS pixels as singles; inline boxes are drawn from
fragments. Each box keeps its used margins, borders and padding, its
collapsing margins as seen from outside, its baselines, its scroll state
and its min/max-content widths (forgotten when it changes). Inline
content is two arrays on the block container: line boxes and fragments
(a byte range of a text box's text, an atomic inline, or an inline box's
part on one line); consecutive text of one box on a line is one
fragment.

`TDocumentLayout` (`Web.Layout.Document`) brings everything up to date:
restyle, rebuild the box children of the elements whose boxes changed
(boxes of untouched subtrees are moved over, not rebuilt), counters,
layout, fixed boxes, scroll extents. `LayoutBox` (`Web.Layout.Dispatch`)
lays out one box for an input (`Web.Layout.Context`: containing block
size, width mode stretch/shrink-to-fit/fixed, the formatting context's
floats and the box's offset in it, the lists absolutely positioned and
fixed boxes go to); a clean box laid out before for the same input whose
layout did not depend on outside floats or containing blocks is skipped,
so relayout after a change touches the changed part and what depends on
its size. A box whose layout put floats into a formatting context outside
it (`bfHasEscapingFloats`: a float in a block that does not contain it)
is never skipped: the context is made anew on every layout, and a skipped
box would leave its floats out of it, so the boxes after it would not
flow around them (4chan's posts were laid over their thumbnails once an
icon in them loaded). A block inside an inline box (block-in-inline)
looks for the floats from its margin edge, as in block flow.

- Block formatting (`Web.Layout.Block`, CSS 2.2 9.4.1, 10.3.3, 10.6.3,
  8.3.1): widths with auto margins, min/max, box-sizing and percentages;
  margin collapsing between siblings, through parents' tops and bottoms
  and through empty blocks, positive and negative; clearance; floats
  (`Web.Layout.Floats`, CSS 2.2 9.5.1) and formatting context roots
  placed beside them; children whose position differs from the guess
  are laid out again when floats could matter; a formatting context
  root's height includes its floats; outside list markers beside the
  first line.
- Inline formatting (`Web.Layout.InlineItems`, `Web.Layout.Inline`): white
  space processing across box boundaries (normal, nowrap, pre, pre-wrap,
  pre-line, break-spaces, tabs), text-transform, letter- and
  word-spacing, greedy line breaking at the break opportunities with
  overflow-wrap/word-break splitting, hanging and dropped collapsible
  spaces, text-indent, text-align (start, end, left, right, center,
  justify, text-align-last, the -webkit- ones HTML's align maps to),
  line heights from each inline box's ascent, descent and half leading
  with vertical-align (baseline, sub, super, text-top, text-bottom,
  middle, lengths, percentages; top and bottom for atomic inlines),
  floats beside or below lines, lines moved below floats too narrow for
  them, static positions, empty lines after forced breaks. A line scanned
  again (moved down past the floats, or broken before a float it had
  passed) does not place its floats a second time: the line state keeps
  the index up to which they are placed. Placing them again once made a
  line that did not fit beside its own float move down for ever, which
  froze the browser on www.wikipedia.org's fundraising banner (reference
  page `floats-wider-than-room`).
- Intrinsic sizes (`Web.Layout.Sizing`): min-content and max-content of
  inline content, block children, flex containers, tables and replaced
  boxes; shrink-to-fit.
- Positioning (`Web.Layout.Positioned`, CSS 2.2 10.3.7, 10.6.4):
  relative offsets, absolute boxes against the padding box of the
  nearest positioned block (left/right/width and top/bottom/height
  constraints, static positions, auto margins centering), fixed boxes
  against the viewport; sticky boxes are laid out as relative ones
  without offsets and moved when painted (below).
- Replaced elements (`Web.Layout.Replaced`): intrinsic sizes from the
  image (or 300x150, or the controls' font-based sizes), the ratio kept
  when one side or a min/max applies; object-fit and object-position
  when painting.
- Flexbox (`Web.Layout.Flex`, CSS Flexbox 1 section 9): flex base sizes,
  automatic minimum sizes, lines, the flexible length resolution loop
  with freezing, cross sizes, align-content, stretch, auto margins,
  justify-content, align-items/align-self with baselines, gaps, order,
  reversed directions and wrap-reverse.
- Grid (`Web.Layout.Grid`, CSS Grid 1 in its basic form): explicit
  tracks from grid-template-columns/rows (lengths, percentages, fr,
  auto, min-content, max-content, minmax(), fit-content(), repeat() with
  counts and auto-fill/auto-fit) and grid-template-areas; placement by
  line numbers (negative from the end), spans and area names, the rest
  by the sparse auto-placement cursor in row or column flow; implicit
  tracks from grid-auto-rows/columns; track sizing (fixed, intrinsic
  from the items' min/max-content contributions with spanning items
  spread, growth to the limits, fr sharing with the minimum kept, auto
  tracks stretched); columns first, rows from the items laid out at
  their widths; justify/align-self and -items (stretch, start, center,
  end), justify/align-content, gaps.
- Tables (`Web.Layout.Table`): automatic layout in brief (grid with
  colspan/rowspan, header groups first and footers last, column
  min/max from cells, spanning cells spread, distribution by what each
  column can still use, row heights, cells stretched to their rows with
  vertical-align, border-spacing, captions above or below the grid).
- Overflow: boxes whose overflow is not visible clip their contents and
  (except overflow: clip) are scroll containers; their scrollable
  overflow is computed after layout.

`Web.Layout.Dump` writes the layout tree as text (box kind, element,
border box in document coordinates, lines and fragments) for the tests.

**Inline SVG** (`Web.Svg.InlineImages`): an outermost `<svg>` is a
replaced box whose image is its subtree drawn by libsvg. The DOM's SVG
elements and text are copied into libsvg's nodes with the styles libweb
computed (page sheets, presentation attributes, inheritance from the
page); libsvg asks back for the styles of content a `<use>`
instantiates (`TDocumentStyler.ResolveStyleUnder`, which also parses
the hints of elements in a hidden sprite sheet), for glyphs (libweb's
font matching) and for elements named by id outside the subtree (a
page's sprite of symbols). The box tree builder keeps one image per
element and makes it again when a signature of the subtree (nodes,
attributes, text, style objects) changes, keeping the replaced one
until the next replacement; images are drawn when painted, at the size
shown. Without width and height the box takes the SVG's natural size
(300 x 150, or the viewBox's ratio within it).

### Painting and hit testing (Web.Paint)

`Web.Paint.Builder` turns the laid out tree into a display list
(`Web.Paint.DisplayList`: small records of one kind each, bounds in
document CSS pixels, color, source box, and an index into side arrays
for radii, border sides, text runs, images, gradients, shadows and
strings) in the painting order of CSS 2.2 Appendix E: each stacking
context paints its background, negative z-index contexts, block
backgrounds in tree order, floats, inline content (inline boxes'
backgrounds and borders on each line, text with decorations and a
text-shadow copy, atomic inlines, replaced content), positioned
descendants with z-index auto/0 in tree order, positive z-index, then
outlines. Floats and atomic inlines paint as if they were stacking
contexts; positioned boxes with z-index auto paint their own content
there, while their positioned descendants are layers of the enclosing
stacking context (a z-index: 100 menu inside position: relative goes
over a later z-index: 1 box). A transform's translations (translate(),
translateX/Y, translate3d, a matrix that only translates, the translate
property; percentages of the border box) move the box like a relative
offset (`Web.Layout.Transforms`), so it is painted, hit and measured
there; a change of them lays the box out again (scMove). Any other
transform (scale, rotate, skew, matrix, the rotate and scale
properties, 3D functions flattened to the plane by
`Css.TransformMatrices`: matrix3d's 2D part, rotateX/Y as the squash
their projection gives, translateZ and perspective dropped) is one
matrix about transform-origin (of the border box) and the box's
stacking context is a transform group (`diPushTransform`, the matrix in
the list's `Transforms`; its bounds: what the group draws). The raster
draws the group untransformed into a surface covering only what can
show through the clip (the clip mapped back through the matrix, within
the bounds, at most 8192 px a side) and composites it through the
matrix with libdrawing's pattern fill (sampled between pixels unless the
matrix is a whole-pixel translation). Hit testing maps the point
through the inverse (clips outside the group are tested where they
were pushed), and getBoundingClientRect gives the bounds of the box
after its and its ancestors' transforms (`TransformRectangle`). Overflow clips become clip
pairs (rounded with border-radius), scroll containers move their
contents, opacity becomes a group, fixed boxes are marked to ignore the
viewport's scroll. Sticky boxes (`Web.Paint.Sticky`, CSS Positioned
Layout 3.4) keep their insets from the scrollport's edges while their
containing block (its content box less their margins) is in view:
under the viewport the list holds a sticky push/pop with those limits
and insets and painting and hit testing work out the offset for the
scroll offset of the moment; inside an inner scroll container (whose
offset is known when the list is built) the offset is applied then.
Masks (`mask-image`, `-position`, `-size`, `-repeat`, `-origin`,
`-clip`, `-mode`, the `mask` shorthand and the `-webkit-` names) are a
mask group: its image layers (url() images and gradients, laid out like
background layers) drawn first, then the content, composited through
the layers' alpha; an image not loaded (or not decodable) masks
everything out, as the spec says (Wikipedia's icons are masks of SVG
images over currentColor). The root's (or body's) background paints the canvas.
Backgrounds have all their layers: color, url() images (sized with
background-size auto/cover/contain/lengths, positioned, repeated) and
gradients (`Web.Paint.Gradients`: linear and radial, repeating,
directions, angles, corners, shapes, sizes, positions, stop fixup,
premultiplied sRGB), clipped by background-clip and origin.

`Web.Paint.Raster` draws a list with libdrawing onto a surface showing
the viewport, for a damaged rectangle only (everything outside it is
skipped), at the device scale and the viewport's scroll offset:
coverage-shaped (anti-aliased) rectangles with elliptical corners (a
libdrawing addition), borders of every style (solid, dashed, dotted,
double, groove, ridge, inset, outset; one ring when rounded), glyphs from
libfont's glyph cache, images scaled and tiled (a scalable image, SVG,
drawn again at the device size of the tile instead, so it stays crisp at
any zoom and pixel ratio), gradients per pixel, box
shadows as a blurred coverage mask (outer and inset), the controls
(check boxes, radio buttons, meters, text field values), clip regions,
opacity groups and masks on transparent surfaces as big as their clip
(not the whole surface) and rounded clips composited through their
coverage.

`TDocumentPainter` (`Web.Paint.Painter`) keeps a layout's display list,
rebuilt when the layout's `PaintVersion` moved, and hit tests on the
same list (every box adds a hit area; clips, fixed and sticky boxes respected):
the topmost node at a viewport point, its element and box.

### Resources: what the loader supplies

`TDocumentResources` (`Web.Layout.Resources`, found or made with
`DocumentResourcesOf(Document)`) is how the loader (Web.Loading) hands
results to styling and layout without either knowing the other:

- `SetElementStyleSheet(LinkElement, Sheet)`: the sheet of a
  `<link rel=stylesheet>` (parsed with libcss's `ParseStyleSheet(Text,
  coAuthor, Url)`), taken over; nil removes it. `AddUserStyleSheet`.
  Imported sheets are hung on their `TCssImportRule.StyleSheet`, then
  `StyleSheetsChanged`. `OnImportsNeeded(Sheet, StyleElement)` asks for
  the imports of sheets made from `<style>` elements.
- `SetElementImage(Element, Image)`: an `<img>`'s (`<input type=image>`,
  `<object>`, `<video poster>`) decoded `TImage`, taken over.
- `SetUrlImage(Url, Image)` for url() in style (backgrounds, ...): the
  layout asks through `OnImageNeeded(Url, BaseUrl)` once per URL text (as
  written; BaseUrl is what it is relative to), the loader answers with
  SetUrlImage under the same URL text, now or later.
- `SetElementImage(Element, Image, NaturalWidth, NaturalHeight)`: with
  the natural size the loader computed (a downscaled image, a srcset
  density), which replaced boxes take as their intrinsic size.
- `FontsChanged` / `NotifyFontsChanged`: the process's font library
  gained web fonts; every layout lays out again (`rcFonts`).
- `FreeDocumentResources(Document)` when the document goes.

The sink that fills them is `TLayoutResourceSink`
(`Web.Loading.LayoutSink`): the loader's deliveries go to the active
document's resources (others are dropped): link sheets, the imports of
`<style>` sheets (asked of the loader with `LoadImportsOf`, then
`StyleSheetsChanged`; the styler indexes its sheets again when told,
since an import hangs on a sheet already in use), images with their
natural size, url() images fetched when the layout first asks (no-cors,
sniffed, decoded on the page thread, given under the URL text as
written), and @font-face sources: TrueType, OpenType (TrueType or CFF
outlines), collections, WOFF 1 (`Web.Text.Woff` unwraps it with
libcompression's zlib) and WOFF2 (`Web.Text.Woff2`: libcompression's
Brotli, then the glyf and loca tables rebuilt from the transformed
glyf's streams of contour and point counts, flags, coordinate
triplets, composite data, boxes and instructions, the loca format
written into head, and hmtx's left side bearings from the glyphs'
xMin when the transform left them out) join the font library under the
rule's family, weight and style; the fonts made from styles then pick
their faces again in place (`RefreshTextFonts`: no font object goes,
so display lists keep valid pointers) and every layout measures again.
Web fonts are process-wide rather than per document. `SetViewport`
gives the loader's media environment (link media, srcset, sizes).

Changes notify the layout (styles become dirty, replaced boxes take
their images and are laid out again, the display list is rebuilt).

### The web view's API

    Layout := TDocumentLayout.Create(Document);   { resources found by document }
    Layout.SetViewport(WidthCss, HeightCss, Scale);
    Layout.Update;                                 { after any change; NeedsUpdate says if one is due }
    Painter := TDocumentPainter.Create(Layout);
    Painter.Paint(Surface, DamagedDeviceRect);     { the surface shows the viewport }
    Hit := Painter.HitTest(XCss, YCss);            { Hit.Node, Hit.Element, Hit.Box }
    Layout.ScrollContainers                        { viewport first: rects, scroll sizes, offsets }
    Layout.SetScrollOffset(NodeOrNil, X, Y); Layout.GetScrollOffset(...)
    Layout.SetElementStates(Element, [esHover, esFocus ...])
    Layout.DocumentWidth / DocumentHeight / NodeBounds(Node, ...) / PaintVersion
    Layout.DisplayListVersion                      { PaintVersion less the viewport's scrolls }

DOM changes reach the layout through the document observer, so a web
view only calls Update (and repaints when PaintVersion moved).

### Tests and webrender

`make web-layout-test` (in `make test`) builds tools/WebLayoutTest on the
host with libcss, libfont, libdrawing and libimage. It lays out the
reference pages of `tools/WebTest/render` (block margins, inline text,
floats, positioning, lists and generated content, flex, grid, tables, replaced
elements and controls, legacy attributes and overflow, painting, inline
SVG with a sprite of symbols and SVG images) and
compares their layout tree dumps with the `.txt` files beside them
(`make web-layout-update` rewrites those; look at the difference and at
the PNGs before committing); checks that incremental restyle and
relayout after DOM changes (classes, inserted and removed elements,
text, display changes, :hover, the viewport size) give the tree a fresh
layout gives and skip clean boxes; hit testing; painting (known pixels:
backgrounds, borders, canvas, z-order, opacity, clipping, scrolling, the
device scale; a damaged rectangle painted alone equal to the full
paint); CSSOM changes restyling (an appended rule indexed at once, a
rule changed in place, a deleted rule, an adopted sheet); transforms
(rotation, scale, skew and a flattened 3D turn by their pixels, hit
testing through them, transformed bounds); animations and transitions
sampled at fixed times of an injected clock (opacity half way and three
quarters, kept at the end, a spinner's quarter turn, a color transition
from the old value through the middle to the new, their end events);
and reports the speed and memory of a 1000 paragraph page (on
the build machine about 30 ms to lay out 8000 nodes, one box per node,
10 display items per paragraph).

`webrender [-w WIDTH] [-h HEIGHT] [-s SCALE] [-f FONTDIR] [-l] [-t]
PAGE.html [OUT.png]` (in /bin, and `make webrender` on the host as
build/tools/webrender with `-f userland/fonts`) renders a page to a PNG
(-t: the whole document) or prints its layout tree (-l); stylesheets and
images referred to by relative URLs are read from beside the page.

### webbrowse: real sites on the host

`make webbrowse` (not in `make test`) builds `build/tools/webbrowse`
(tools/WebBrowse): the engine as the browser runs it, on the Linux host.
A `TWebPage` over a network context whose libhttp client connects with
the host's sockets (`WebBrowse.HostNetwork`: getaddrinfo, a non-blocking
connect within the timeout, libtls with `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`
and session resumption, ALPN h2), the layout resource sink, page
scripting, and the event loop driven like the web view drives it (tasks
in 12 ms slices, a frame every 16 ms: rendering steps, style, layout,
then the viewport painted, which is when url() images are asked for).
It runs until the load event and quiet (no fetch, no url() image, no
ready task, no layout due for `-q` ms) or the timeout:

    webbrowse [-o OUT.png] [-w W] [-h H] [-s SCALE] [-y SCROLL] [--full]
      [--resize WxH] [-l LAYOUT|-] [--dom HTML|-] [-c] [-n] [--live] [-p] [-m]
      [-t SECONDS] [-q MS] [--stall S] [--no-script] [-e JS] [--do STEP]...
      [--hover N] [--profile] [-f FONTDIR] [-v] URL

`-n` prints every request (start, time to the head, total, status,
protocol, destination, bytes, outcome) from a fetch monitor
(`Web.Fetch.Monitors`: the fetcher tells a `TFetchMonitor` when a fetch
starts, responds, fails, ends or is cancelled); `-p` the time in each
phase (`Web.Profiling`: the engine marks HTML parsing, style sheet
parsing, style, box building, layout, painting, script and other tasks;
nested phases are charged their own time only; off unless a program
starts profiling with a fine clock); `-c` console messages; `-m` peak
memory; `--hover N` moves the pointer over the page as the web view
does (:hover on the chain under it) and times each move; `--resize`
changes the viewport once quiet; `-e` evaluates script once quiet;
`--do` steps are what a user does then, each once the page is quiet
again (or after 10 s): `eval:JS`, `type:TEXT` (`\n` is Enter; a key
every 60 ms), `key:NAME` (KeyboardEvent codes with `ctrl+`, `shift+`,
`alt+`), `click:SELECTOR`, `wait:MS`, `shot:FILE.png`. Keys and clicks
go through `WebBrowse.Input` the way the web view gives them (keydown,
keypress, `WebView.FieldEditing`, keyup; Enter submits implicitly;
links followed), so a search can be typed, suggested, submitted and a
result clicked on the host:

    webbrowse -c -n --do 'type:free pascal' --do 'shot:typed.png' \
      --do 'key:Enter' --do 'shot:results.png' https://duckduckgo.com/

It sends the browser's user agent (`Web.UserAgent`). A timeout says why
the page never went quiet (a task ready, layout due). A watchdog thread (`WebBrowse.Watchdog`) reports a page thread making no
progress for `--stall` seconds: its phase stack and detail (the script
or sheet being worked on) and its stack, sampled by interrupting it
with SIGUSR1 and walking its frame pointers (`WebBrowse.Sampler`,
x86-64; the tool keeps frame pointers and line information), and ends
the process after a minute more. `--profile` samples that stack every
millisecond while the page thread works and prints the functions it
was in (self) and under (total), symbolized from the line information
and `nm` for the run-time library.

On the build machine Wikipedia's Main Page (1280 px) loads in about 1.3
s, most of it network: 30 ms of style, 25 ms of layout, longest frame
about 50 ms; the Pascal article (25000 px tall) about 90 ms of style and
80 ms of layout in all, the longest frame about 90 ms (the first full
style and layout); the Linux article (34000 px, 2 MB of HTML) about 110
ms each. A pointer move over an article costs about 2 ms.

On top of the pointer steps (`WebBrowse.Pointer` over libwebview's
page selection), two steps also take another shape of argument:
`scroll:top` and `scroll:bottom` put the viewport there (a number is
the wheel's DY), and `hover:SELECTOR` moves the pointer to the middle of
the first element matching, scrolled into view (X,Y is a point).
`scrollby:DY` scrolls the viewport itself, `hoverat:X,Y` is
`hover:X,Y`, `back` and `forward` go through the session history.
`--patience MS` is how long a step waits for quiet before it goes on
(10 s); an endless animation alone does not keep a page from being
quiet.

#### Comparing common sites with a reference browser

`scripts/compare-sites.py` (not in `make test`: it needs the network)
takes the pages of `scripts/compare-sites.list` (about 27 common pages
that need no login: Wikipedia, search engines, news sites, shops,
project sites) and, for each, at 1280x800 and 400x800:

- renders it with webbrowse (`--webbrowse BINARY`: a copy keeps runs
  apart from builds) and records the load time, console errors, failed
  requests, crashes (a signal, a run-time error, an engine exception
  in the output), hangs (the watchdog, or no end within the time-out
  and a grace) and time-outs;
- renders it with the installed Firefox (`scripts/firefox_reference.py`,
  driven over its Marionette protocol with no extra packages: headless,
  a profile and port per worker, overlay scroll bars so the page gets
  the whole width, the window grown until the viewport is exactly the
  size asked, a narrower viewport than the window allows made by
  narrowing the page's browser element, the page left 3 s after its
  load to settle). The pictures are kept between runs
  (`--refresh-reference` makes them again), so runs before and after a
  change compare against the same pictures;
- scores the difference (Pillow: both pictures in gray, per 16 px block
  the difference of the means and of the contrast; 0 alike, 100 nothing
  alike; also per region of a 3 x 3 grid) and writes a heat map;
- drives the page like a user in webbrowse (the smoke test): marks up
  to six visible links and buttons, three same-site links and the first
  search box with a script, scrolls down to the bottom in steps and back
  up, hovers the marked elements and a grid of points, drags a
  selection, types into the search box, follows each marked link,
  scrolls and hovers there and goes back. A crash or hang fails it.

Everything goes into the folder given with `--out` (outside the
repository: nothing it fetched is committed): the pictures, the logs,
`results.json`, and `report.txt` / `report.html` with the pages by
score (`--baseline OLD/results.json` puts the earlier scores beside
them). Problems found are reduced to small cases in the host tests
(tools/WebTest/render, WebLayoutTest, WebScriptTest, WebLoadTest,
JavaScriptTest).

`scripts/qemu-browser-smoke.py ESP SYSTEM-DISK OUT [NAME ...]` does the
user's part with the real browser: it boots the system under QEMU (KVM
with `ACCEL=kvm`), waits for the network, starts the display server,
and for each page opens `/app/browser/browser` on it, scrolls with the
wheel, moves the tablet over a grid of points, drags a selection,
clicks three points and goes back with Alt+Left, then checks the
browser still runs and nothing panicked; it keeps a screen dump of each
page after loading and after the steps.

### Not done yet (layout and painting)

Grid's subgrid, dense packing, baseline alignment, named lines and the
full intrinsic track sizing algorithm, the fixed table
layout and collapsing borders (laid out as separate borders without
spacing), multi-column layout, writing modes and bidirectional text
(rtl only flips text-align), shaping beyond kerning (ligatures, complex
scripts: Arabic draws unjoined), emoji ZWJ sequences and flags (their
parts draw one by one), a collection's face chosen by language (its
first is used), ::first-line and ::first-letter, inline boxes
split around blocks (blocks inside inline boxes take lines of their own
instead), relative positioning of inline boxes,
perspective and preserve-3d, filters, blend modes, clip-path, border-image, conic
gradients, text-shadow blur, outlines following border radii, the
`visibility: collapse` of table parts, incremental display list updates
(it is rebuilt whole when anything changes; scrolling the viewport does
not rebuild it).

`make web-load-test` (in `make test`) builds `tools/WebLoadTest` with
libhttp, libcss, libimage and what they need, with range checks. It
checks the event loop with a hand-driven clock (tasks against
microtasks, sources, timer order, clearing, nesting clamps for
timeouts and intervals, frame callbacks, 200 tasks posted from another
thread, dropping a group, the id map), the fetch layer's rules (MIME
types, data: URLs and base64, sniffing, every referrer policy, HSTS,
CSP, mixed content, CORS and preflights), the fetcher against an
in-process site (a libhttp connector of in-memory pipes to HTTP/1.1
server threads whose routes can send bodies in pieces behind a gate:
the fields sent, redirects and their limits, CORS with a cached
preflight, mixed content blocked before any request, HSTS, schemes,
sniffing, nosniff, file: in pieces, cancelling), and documents through
a navigable with a recording sink, observer and script executor: the
first piece parsed before the rest arrives, readyState and events in
order, style sheets with imports, media, alternate and disabled holding
the load event, fonts, srcset at a pixel ratio of 2, downscaling, the
favicon, a late meta charset restarting the parse, text and error
documents, downloads, scripts in order with the preload scanner
fetching ahead, unload events, and history (fragments, back, forward,
reload). Then a page rendered end to end: a navigable with the layout's
sink loads a page with a linked sheet, a `<style>` with an @import, an
image, a url() background and web fonts (TrueType and WOFF made from
DejaVu Sans Mono) from the in-process site; the layout dump has the
sizes those give, the background and the image are painted, and the
web fonts measure. And a scripted page through `TPageScriptExecutor`:
inline, external and deferred scripts in order, document.write,
DOMContentLoaded and load at the page's listeners and handlers,
setTimeout, document.cookie without the HttpOnly cookie, readyState and
location, an onclick attribute, alert and pushState.

Then a fuzz test of editing (`WebLoadTest.Editing`): a hostile page
(`tools/WebLoadTest/editing-fuzz.html`) whose listeners replace,
remove, move, hide, retype and disable the fields being typed into,
rebuild forms, clone its body and move the focus during keydown,
keypress, keyup, input, focus and change events (and in microtasks,
timers and frames after them) is given 2500 seeded random key presses,
edits and clicks the way the web view gives them (webbrowse's
`TPageInput`: keydown, keypress, `WebView.FieldEditing`, keyup;
mousedown, focus, mouseup, click; change when the focus leaves a
changed field), with layout, painting, hit testing, the caret's reads
and both collectors between steps. It passes when it survives with
every field's selection within its value, the document whole, the page
not navigated (every submission cancelled or of a detached form) and no
uncaught script errors. `WebLoadTest editing` runs it alone,
`WEB_EDITING_VERBOSE=1` prints a line a step, `JS_GC_STRESS=1` makes
the engines collect every 16 KiB. It found the script clones that ran
again, a detached form submitting, and empty root arrays failing range
checks in the collector.

And a fuzz test of the pointer (`WebLoadTest.Pointer`): a long generated
page (`tools/WebLoadTest/pointer-fuzz.html`: a sticky header and
section titles, a fixed footer, floats, transformed, animated and
absolutely placed paragraphs, an inner scroll container, a frame) whose
listeners on every mouse event, selectionchange, timer and animation
frame read sizes (laying the page out inside the event), remove,
replace, split, merge, move and hide the text under the pointer and in
the selection, set the selection (also into a detached tree), delete it
from the document and scroll, is given 3000 seeded random moves,
presses, drags (past the viewport's edges, the wheel turned in the
middle), releases, double and triple clicks, wheel steps, resizes,
copies and select-alls through `TPagePointer` (`WebBrowse.Pointer`: the
web view's pointer steps over its `TPageSelection`), with the layout
brought up to date or left behind (as the web view puts a slow layout
off), painting, hit testing, the selection's rectangles and both
collectors between steps; then 600 more with the engines collecting
every 16 KiB; then a wheel storm of 2000 steps, most of them bursts of
10 to 60 wheel steps both ways with the pointer moving over the page,
the layout left behind, and tasks, rendering steps, animations, hit
tests and resizes in between. It passes when the document's selection stays in the
document, the view's selection in its current index, its text and
rectangles readable, and no script error is uncaught. `WebLoadTest
pointer` runs it alone, `WEB_POINTER_VERBOSE=1` prints a line a step.
It found a removed frame's freed document painted from a stale box and
a steep edge rounded to cell -1 in libdrawing's rasterizer.
webbrowse's `--do` drives the same pointer on real sites: `scroll:DY`,
`hover:X,Y`, `press:X,Y`, `move:X,Y`, `release:X,Y`,
`drag:X1,Y1,X2,Y2`, `dblclick:X,Y`, `tripleclick:X,Y`, `selectall` and
`copy` (prints the selected text).

`make web-script-test` (in `make test`) builds `tools/WebScriptTest`
with libjavascript, libcss and libhttp's URL units. Each
`scripts/*.js` runs in a fresh window over its `scripts/*.html` page (or
an empty one) with a test environment (timers fired as tasks, external
scripts served from a table, navigations recorded) and makes its checks
with `check()`: tree changes and serialization, events (order, once,
stopping, canceling, handlers, the window in the path, exceptions in
listeners), wrapper identity and prototype chains, selectors,
reflection and form controls, parsing with scripts and document.write,
MutationObserver records and their microtask, ranges (live adjustment,
the content operations) and the selection, the CSSOM, MessagePorts
between realms and frames by name, TextEncoder/TextDecoder,
atob/btoa, structuredClone, URL and URLSearchParams, the window and the
timers. The Pascal side checks that unreachable wrappers are collected
and their nodes freed, that expandos and listeners live while their node
is in the document, that detached cycles go in one collection, events
made by native code, events the engine fired kept by a listener past
their dispatch and a collection (the DuckDuckGo crash) and an event
